account.canonical_name: Administration for a Healthy America (agency total)
account.notes: Proposed in the FY2026 and FY2027 budget requests only; never reported by a committee or enacted (P.L. 119-75 has no such heading). The committee tables print it only in the request column, as the request's funding 'not displayed under other HHS accounts below' (H.Rept. 119-271 p.334 footnote 1/): the tables show most of the proposed AHA under HRSA, SAMHSA and the other legacy lines. Derived rollup (agency). H.Rept. 119-696 prints no plain total, only 'Administration for a Healthy America, Discretionary 1/', recorded as the headline there.

relationships.evidence: Proposed, not enacted. FY2026 Budget Appendix (BUDGET-2026-APP) pp. 332, 338, 339, 346: 'In 2026 HRSA will be reorganized into the Agency [p.339: Administration] for a Healthy America to improve coordination of health resources for Americans.' Repeated for 2027 in the FY2027 Appendix (BUDGET-2027-APP) pp. 434, 439, 449. P.L. 119-75 keeps HRSA. Also FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)' -- names HRSA.
relationships.other_name: Health Resources and Services Administration (agency total)

relationships.evidence: Proposed, not enacted. FY2026 Budget Appendix p.360: 'In 2026 SAMHSA will be reorganized into the Agency for a Healthy America to improve coordination of health resources for Americans.' FY2027 Appendix p.464 repeats it for 2027. P.L. 119-75 keeps SAMHSA. Also FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)' -- names SAMHSA.
relationships.other_name: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (agency total)

relationships.evidence: Proposed, not enacted (FY2026 President's Budget). FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)'. p.13 (PDF p.3), Environmental Health: 'National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS): $594.1 million'. Amount match: H.Rept. 119-271 p.344 FY 2026 Request, NIEHS 594,086 (thousands) = $594.1M rounded. The FY2027 request instead proposes moving NIEHS into CDC (a placement note on the account, not a relationship). P.L. 119-75 keeps NIEHS under NIH.
relationships.other_name: National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences

relationships.evidence: Proposed, not enacted (FY2026 President's Budget). relationships.evidence: Proposed, not enacted (FY2026 President's Budget). FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)'. p.13 (PDF p.3), Environmental Health: 'Occupational Safety and Health: $73.2 million ... in discretionary funding to support select programs in worker safety and health, including the National Mesothelioma Registry and Tissue Bank, National Firefighter Registry for Cancer, and Mining Research'. Amount match: H.Rept. 119-271 p.342 FY 2026 Request, National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health 73,200 (thousands) = $73.2M: the whole NIOSH request. P.L. 119-75 keeps NIOSH under CDC.

relationships.evidence: Proposed, not enacted (FY2026 President's Budget). FY2026 AHA Congressional Justification (SRC-CJ-AHA-FY2026) p.11 (PDF p.1), Overview of Budget: 'the AHA Budget consolidates and streamlines chronic care and disease prevention programs across the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (OASH), Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), and several centers and programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)'. p.14 (PDF p.4), Environmental Health: 'Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program Act (EEOICPA): $50.8 million in mandatory funding (post-sequester)'. Amount match, pre- vs post-sequester: H.Rept. 119-271 p.342 FY 2026 Request prints 55,358 (thousands), the appropriation before sequestration; 55,358 - 50,800 = 4,558 (8.2%) sequestered. The FY2026 Budget Appendix (BUDGET-2026-APP p.333), AHA's proposed Environmental Health account (075-0386), appropriates the same '$55,358,000' for EEOICPA and shows, in $ millions for 2026: mandatory appropriation 55, permanently reduced -4, mandatory total 51 (= $50.8M rounded). P.L. 119-75 keeps it under CDC.
